64629.subject: Government
64629.question_text: The highest authority in the Yoruba pre-colonial era was the _____
64629.explanation: The Oba is the highest authority in the Yoruba Kingdom. He is both the political and spiritual head of the Oyo kingdom popularly known as the Alaafin of Oyo.

64630.subject: Government
64630.explanation: Unity in diversity is a phrase that signifies unity among people with diverse cultural, and religious beliefs, social status, and other demographic differences. Nigeria is a nation with a large population consisting of people with different beliefs, traditions, religions,

64631.subject: Government
64631.question_text: One of the constitutional requirements for the registration of political parties in Nigeria is ______
64631.explanation: The Party in its formation must provide evidence of ownership or rental of an office in at least 24 States of the Federation, with its headquarters located in the Federal Capital Territory.

options.text: provision for review of party manifesto
national presence in the federal capital territory

64636.subject: Government
64636.question_text: The Security Council of the United Nations Organization has
64636.explanation:
The Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent members with veto power.

The five permanent members of the UN Security Council, often referred to as the P5, are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. These countries have the privilege of veto power, which means that any substantive resolution cannot be adopted if one or more of them cast a negative vote. Additionally, there are ten non-permanent members elected for two-year terms by the General Assembly.

64650.subject: Government
64650.question_text: The oversight function is performed by the
64650.explanation: Legislative oversight is one of the methods of checks and balances. The Legislature checks on the executive through budget approval, committee hearings, confirmation of appointments made by the executive, etc.

64663.subject: Government
64663.question_text: Before the emergence of OAU as a regional body, Nigeria belonged to
64663.explanation: Before the emergence of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) as a regional body, Nigeria belonged to the Monrovia group.  Monrovia group consisted of African states that favoured a gradual approach to continental unity and integration. This contrasted with the more radical approach of the Casablanca group.

64664.subject: Government
64664.question_text: The political rights of a citızen include the
64664.explanation: The right to vote is one of the political rights of a citizen. A citizen who is of legal age must be allowed to vote in any election.

64666.subject: Government
64666.question_text: One of the features of rule of law is that an
64666.explanation: One of the features of the rule of law is that the accused must receive a fair hearing before he can be considered guilty of a crime.

options.text: accused is a culprit before trial

64667.subject: Government
64667.question_text: The first Legislative Councıl in Nigeria was established by
64667.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 established the first legislative council in Nigeria.

64669.subject: Government
64669.question_text: An electoral system in which the winner must secure more than 50% of the vote is described as a/an
64669.explanation: The electoral system in which the winner must secure more than 50% of the vote is described as an "absolute majority," This means the candidate or option needs to obtain more than half of the total votes cast to win.

64670.subject: Government
64670.question_text: A group of people with different natures, opinions, and goals with complicated networks of social relation
64670.explanation: A group of people with different natures, opinions, and goals with complicated networks of social relation is referred to as a society.

64671.subject: Government
64671.question_text: A political system built around land ownership is called
64671.explanation: Feudalism is a form of government that is based on land ownership. The owners of the land in a feudal system are referred to as Lords and Vassals and they are at the top of the feudal hierarchy. Beneath them are Peasants and Serfs who work the land in exchange for wages, housing and security from the Lords and Vassals.

64674.subject: Government
64674.explanation: One of the merits of a one-party system is that it helps to prevent economic waste. With only one party in a state, resources do not have to be diverted to conducting elaborate elections in the selection of leaders.

64675.subject: Government
64675.question_text: The French colonial policy aimed at changing Africans into French men was the policy of
64675.explanation: The policy of assimilation was the official colonial policy of the French administration in West Africa. The system involved the imposition of French culture on West African culture. It was meant to substitute the culture, language, religion, law, mode of dressing, etc. of the people of West Africa with that of the French people.

64676.subject: Government
64676.question_text: A system of government in which a single person or a group who governs has unlimited power is a
64676.explanation: Autocracy a system of government by one person with absolute power.

64677.subject: Government
64677.question_text: The Judicial Service Commission is vested with the power to recommend suitable persons for appointment of the _____
64677.explanation: The Judicial Service Commission (JSC) in Nigeria plays a role in judicial appointments. However, when it comes to federal judicial appointments, especially for high-level positions like the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), the National Judicial Council (NJC) is primarily responsible for recommending suitable candidates to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, upon the recommendations of the Judicial Service Commission. The Judicial Service Commission is vested with the power to recommend suitable persons for appointment as the Chief Justice of Nigeria to the National Judicial Council (NJC), who then offers such recommendations to the President.

64678.subject: Government
64678.question_text: A policy formulated to guide relations with other nations is called
64678.explanation: Foreign policy is a government's strategy in dealing with other nations

64684.subject: Government
64684.question_text: A major consequence of the privatization exercise in Nigeria is
64684.explanation: The sole aim of Privatization is profit-making. There is often a reduction of costs or spending and  mass retrenchment of labour in response to economic difficulty.

options.text: the collapse of the Nigerian economy

64686.subject: Government
64686.question_text: The highest body which performed legislative functions under Babangida Regime was
64686.explanation:
The Supreme Military Council, SMC was the top highest organ of the Federal Government of Nigeria in the military regimes of Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi, General Yakubu Gowon, Murtala Mohammed, General Obasanjo and Major General Muhammadu Buhari.
The body was instituted in 1966 by the administration of Aguiyi Ironsi deriving power from statute 8 of decree 1, it was later replaced as the highest body in a military regime by President Ibrahim Babangida in 1985 who created the Armed Forces Ruling Council.

64689.subject: Government
64689.question_text: The aim of the International Labour Organization includes
64689.explanation: The International Labour Organization ( ILO) is a United Nations agency whose mandate is to advance social and economic justice through setting international labour standards. Founded in October 1919 under the League of Nations, it is the first and oldest specialized agency of the UN.

options.text: coordinating the activities of organized agencies

64693.subject: Government
64693.question_text: One of these is a major problem of the Nigerian civil service
64693.explanation: Inadequate personnel refers to a significant challenge where there is a shortage of qualified and skilled personnel to effectively carry out the functions and duties of the civil service. This shortage can lead to inefficiencies, delays in service delivery and difficulties in implementing policies effectively. Addressing this issue typically involves efforts to recruit and train more personnel, improve retention rates, and ensure that the civil service has the capacity to meet the demands of governance and public service delivery.

64695.subject: Government
64695.question_text: The basic unit of every political organization in the Igbo pre-colonial era was the
64695.explanation: The Family Group is one of the most recognized institutions in pre-colonial Igbo society as the basic unit of every political institution.

64697.subject: Government
64697.question_text: The defence pact between Nigeria and Britain was cancelled in the year
64697.explanation: The defence pact between Nigeria and Britain, known as the Anglo-Nigerian Defense Pact, was indeed cancelled in 1962. This agreement, signed in 1960 shortly after Nigeria gained independence from Britain, allowed British military presence and assistance in Nigeria. However, Nigeria sought to assert its sovereignty more fully, leading to negotiations in 1962 that resulted in the cancellation of the pact. This move was part of Nigeria's broader efforts to establish its independence and autonomy in foreign and defence policies following decolonization.

64699.subject: Government
64699.question_text: The absence of an independent judiciary is a feature of
64699.explanation: In an oligarchy, power is concentrated in the hands of a few, and there is often a lack of an independent judiciary to check the power of the ruling group.

64700.subject: Government
64700.question_text: Nigeria is a major financier of which of the following?
64700.explanation: Nigeria is one of the major financiers and a significant stakeholder in the African Development Bank.

64701.subject: Government
64701.question_text: A constıtution that requires specific statutory procedures for amendment is said to be
64701.explanation: A rigid constitution requires specific and often more complex procedures for amendment, making it more difficult to change.

64702.subject: Government
64702.question_text: The ultimate goal of the nationalists was to
64702.explanation: The primary objective of nationalist movements across Africa, including Nigeria, was to achieve political independence from colonial rule.

64703.subject: Government
64703.question_text: A recurring principal objective of Nigerian foreign policy is
64703.explanation: A consistent and recurring objective of Nigeria’s foreign policy is the promotion of international peace and justice, especially in line with its role in Africa and global organizations. Nigeria has historically contributed to peacekeeping missions and supports peaceful resolution of conflicts.

64705.subject: Government
64705.question_text: The operations of a pressure group can be hindered by
64705.explanation: Poor leadership can lead to ineffective decision-making, lack of clear direction, and internal conflicts, all of which can hinder the operations of a pressure group.

64708.subject: Government
64708.question_text: The 1976 Local Government Reforms made the Nigerian local government become
64708.explanation: The 1976 Local Government Reforms in Nigeria made significant changes to the local government system. The reforms aimed to make local governments more autonomous by granting them more powers and responsibilities.

66989.subject: Government
66989.question_text: Which of these is not a major characteristic of the rule of law?
66989.explanation: Separation of powers is also called a system of checks and balances because the branches can check up on each other and if any of the branches get too strong, that branch will be balanced by the others. However, it is not a feature of the rule of law.

66990.subject: Government
66990.question_text: Unitary system of government is best applicable to a/an
66990.explanation: An homogeneous state has a single language, belief, culture and ethnicity among its people.

66991.subject: Government
66991.question_text: The ________ as a new policy direction introduced by the French government that was aimed at granting more autonomy to its colonies under pressure from independence movements.
66991.explanation: The loi-cadre ( Reform Act) was a French legal reform passed by the French National Assembly on 23 June 1956. It marked a turning point in relations between France and its overseas empire. Under pressure from independence movements in the colonies, the government transferred a number of powers from Paris to elected territorial governments in French African colonies and also removed remaining voting inequalities by implementing universal suffrage and abolishing the multiple electoral college system.

66992.subject: Government
66992.question_text: On 1 October 1995, Abacha announced a three-year program for return to civilian rule. Parties were allowed to form in July 1998. Which of the following parties was not registered by the Provisional Ruling Council?
66992.explanation: Three parties were registered by the Provisional Ruling Council for participation in local, state and national elections: the All People's Party or APP led by Mahmud Waziri; the People's Democratic Party or PDP led by Soloman Lar; and the Alliance for Democracy or AD, led by Ayo Adebanjo.

66993.subject: Government
66993.question_text: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) has its headquarters in
66993.explanation:
The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID), is the financial institution established by the 15 Member States of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) comprising Benin, Burkina Faso, Capo Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo.
The Bank's headquarters is in Lome, Togolese Republic.

66994.subject: Government
66994.question_text: The conference convened to discuss the provisions of the Macpherson Constitution was held in?
66994.explanation: On the 9th of January, 1950, delegates from the northern, eastern and western regions of Nigeria met as a body in Ibadan to discuss issues on the new constitution Sir Macpherson was drafting (Macpherson constitution of 1951).

66995.subject: Government
66995.question_text: Nigeria's bicameral legislature featuring the House of Senate and House of Representatives is similar to ?
66995.explanation: The USA has both the House of Senate and House of Representatives. The UK has the House of Common and House of Lords instead. China and New Zealand both practise unicameralism.

66996.subject: Government
66996.question_text: The process of pressure groups trying to influence legislation is known as
66996.explanation: Pressure groups are organisations which seek to influence the policies of the government and this process is known as lobbying.

66997.subject: Government
66997.question_text: In a federal system of government, legislative items constitutionally reserved for only the central government fall under the _________ list.
66997.explanation:
Exclusive Legislative List

These are the areas the powers reserved exclusively for the central government are defined. This means that only the central or federal government can legislate on the subjects in the exclusive list. Interference of the regional or state governments on matters in the exclusive list can be declared null and void and unconstitutional.

66998.subject: Government
66998.question_text: Which one of these served as secretary general of the League of nations?
66998.explanation: Joseph Avenol (1879--1952) was a French diplomat who served as the secretary-general of the League of Nations in the years leading up to World War II. He succeeded British diplomat, Eric Drummond.
